misclassified_entities.reason: In precompile context, the caller is another contract within the same EVM execution context. It is internal to the EVM, not an external entity crossing a trust boundary.

This represents the input data to the precompile, which is already within the EVM message context. The data originated from an external source but by the time it reaches the precompile, it's internal call data.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Miner)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block producers create and propose blocks to the network. No authentication of producer identity. Blocks must be fully validated against consensus rules including PoW verification (or ProgPoW). Producer could attempt to manipulate timestamps or include invalid transactions.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer Node
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Anonymous P2P network participant propagating blocks and transactions. No identity verification required. All received data (blocks, headers, transactions) must be fully validated before acceptance.

trusted_external_entities.name: Blob Transaction Submitter
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External user or rollup submitting EIP-4844 blob transactions. Blob data is arbitrary and untrusted. Gas pricing (blob base fee) must be enforced. KZG commitments must be verified.

trusted_external_entities.name: Berlin Network Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peer participating in Berlin-era network. Access list data in transactions must be validated. Peer could send malformed access lists attempting to exploit gas calculation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External account submitting transactions. Transaction signature provides authentication of sender address, but sender intent is not trusted. All transaction fields must be validated including access lists, gas limits, and nonce.

trusted_external_entities.name: Berlin Block Miner
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block producer in Berlin fork. Must include valid access list transactions. Block validation includes checking all access list entries are properly formatted and gas is correctly calculated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Layer 2 Rollup
trusted_external_entities.rationale: L2 solutions deploying RIP precompiles in reserved address range (0x100-0x1ff). Rollups are expected to coordinate via RIP governance process. However, different rollups may implement precompiles differently, requiring validation at cross-rollup boundaries.

trusted_external_entities.name: Smart Contract Caller
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Contract making calls to precompile addresses. Contract code is arbitrary and could be malicious. Precompile must handle all input correctly regardless of caller intent.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block must pass full consensus validation including ProgPoW verification if applicable. Invalid blocks are rejected without affecting node state.
All data from peers must be independently validated. Peer reputation may be tracked but does not reduce validation requirements.
Blob transactions must pay blob base fee. KZG commitments must match blob data. Max blobs per block enforced. Gas calculation includes blob gas.
Access list entries must be valid addresses and storage keys. Gas calculation must account for access list size. Type 1 transactions must be properly formatted.
Block must contain valid type 0 and type 1 transactions. Access list gas costs must be correctly calculated per EIP-2930.
Precompile must handle arbitrary input data. Gas must be sufficient for operation. Output is deterministic based on input.
L2 rollups coordinate via RIP process. Address range 0x100-0x1ff reserved. No L1 enforcement of RIP compliance - trust is social/governance based.
